# 1 Clement Chapter 29 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 29 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_029_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 29

**29:1** So let us draw near to him with purity of soul, lifting up to him clean and unstained hands, and let us love our gentle and compassionate Father who has made us his own chosen people.

**29:2** For this is what is written: "When the Most High divided the nations, when he scattered the children of Adam, he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the angels of God. His people Jacob became the LORD's own portion, and Israel the measuring line of his inheritance."

**29:3** And elsewhere it says: "See, the Lord takes for himself a nation from among the nations, as a man takes the firstfruits from his threshing floor; and the Holy of Holies shall come forth from that nation."

---

*PNEUMA renders the election language accessibly while preserving its weight. "Chosen people" for the church echoes the New Testament (1 Pet 2:9) and brings out the typological point Clement is making.*
